METHOD & SOURCES

About this reference

A selective map of AI system design, supported by primary documentation and illustrative cloud compositions.

Scope and selection

The atlas covers application and system patterns: how inputs, models, retrieval, tools, queues, devices, and review stages fit together. It does not attempt to catalog neural network internals such as transformers or diffusion networks. Patterns were selected for broad applicability, not ranked by measured market share.

Layered and overlapping

The homepage leads to category collections, which lead to shared architecture pages. The six categories mix interaction style, deployment environment, and orchestration as navigational lenses. There are 20 unique patterns; multiple memberships do not create duplicate designs.

Interface and activation are separate

AI work can begin with a user turn, an event, a stream, or a schedule. An agent may continue after a chat ends. A recommendation system may never expose a conversational interface. Several patterns can coexist in one product.

Cloud mappings and notation

The cloud buttons switch between AWS, GCP, and Azure diagrams and service tables. Choices are illustrative; they do not imply identical features, region availability, limits, or prices. Custom application code, human judgment, and local device execution are labeled separately.

Rounded blocks indicate actors, rectangles processing, diamonds decisions, cylinders stored data, and stacked marks queues or streams. Solid arrows trace the primary path; dashed arrows show loops or bypasses. The enclosure is logical scope rather than a cloud network boundary.

Research method

Core references were reviewed October 20, 2026. This complete distribution was assembled October 22, 2026. Examples, tradeoffs, safeguards, measurements, and compositions are editorial synthesis. Verify each service’s current documentation and evaluate representative workloads before implementation.

Read-only and static

All HTML, styles, diagrams, and the small cloud-selection script are self-hosted. The website contains no visitor forms, accounts, cookies, browser storage, tracking, third-party scripts, fonts, or embeds. Changing the cloud selection makes no network requests. With JavaScript disabled, all cloud references remain visible.
